instruction: Using Visual Studio Code, create a Python script named `crypto_volatility_analysis.py` in the `/home/user/analysis_results/crypto_volatility/` directory. In this script: 1) Navigate to `https://www.coinmarketcap.com/` and scrape the top 50 cryptocurrencies by market capitalization, extracting for each: `name`, `symbol`, `price`, `24h_change`, `7d_change`, `market_cap`. 2) Load historical daily price data for each of the top 50 coins (e.g., the last 7 days), compute daily returns and then compute a 7-day volatility measure (standard deviation of daily returns). 3) Add a column `seven_day_volatility` to the dataset and identify the coins with the highest volatility. 4) Save the results to a CSV file named `crypto_volatility.csv` in the same directory with columns: `name`, `symbol`, `price`, `24h_change`, `7d_change`, `market_cap`, `seven_day_volatility`. 5) In the same directory, save a text file named `top_volatile_coins.txt` containing exactly one line formatted as: `Most_Volatile_Coins: <symbol1>,<symbol2>,<symbol3>` (list the top 3 coins by volatility).
